punchline: Thich Nhat Hanh's walk has no destination on purpose, and your lungs decide how many steps each breath gets.
thirty_sec: Thich Nhat Hanh says most of our walking is closer to running. His fix is walking meditation: slow, outdoors, three steps with each in-breath and three with each out-breath. If your lungs want four steps, they get four. Feel your feet meet the ground, stop when a tree or a flower catches you, then start again. The one rule is that you are not trying to arrive anywhere, because he says that is how you lose your steps.
